questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How eight employees left Shockley's lab to found Fairchild Semiconductor
How Shockley's invention of the transistor won him a Nobel Prize
The corporate histories of Raytheon and Beckman Instruments compared
How Intel and AMD grew into leaders of the semiconductor industry
questions.explain: It describes why and how the eight left Shockley Semiconductor in 1957 to found Fairchild.

questions.q: Who funded Shockley's laboratory as a department of his company?
questions.explain: Arnold Beckman, owner of Beckman Instruments, agreed to fund the lab.

questions.q: Which candidate got a salary of $675 a month?
questions.explain: The less-experienced Last got $675, while Kleiner, Noyce and Roberts got $1,000.

questions.q: Where did Kleiner actually go in March 1957 after claiming he would visit an exhibition in Los Angeles?
questions.explain: He flew to New York to seek investors for a new company.

questions.q: Why did Shockley consider Noyce his sole support in the group?
options: Noyce stood behind him and tried to resolve conflicts
Noyce had the deepest background in electronics research
Noyce was the first physicist he recruited from Bell Labs
Noyce led the dissidents pushing for Shockley's replacement
questions.explain: While Moore led the dissidents, Noyce backed Shockley and tried to resolve conflicts.
